note: Advanced singing made musical: a fast run and an octave tune to open the range, then guide tones and improvising over a ii-V-I that the app plays as accompaniment, with the line sung from a staff. The run's range is stated, every target is named with the chord it lands on, and each block says what to sing on.

exercise.title: Guide tones over ii-V-I, then your own line
exercise.focus: Pentatonic run · octave tune · guide tones over Dm7-G7-Cmaj7 · your own line in F
exercise.why: Singing the 3rds and 7ths through a ii-V-I trains you to hear the chord changes.

sections.text: Press Play below to hear the run, then start the mic and sing it lightly on "ah" at the tempo shown. It goes from La below Do up to the high Do, and each pass starts a semitone higher: five passes, the last one reaching the top of your range. Two chords play first to set the key.
Then switch the tune off in the player and sing the run over the chords alone. Ideas: try "ee" or "lip trill", or sing it staccato.
Press Play below to hear a tune that leaps to the octave, then start the mic and sing it on "oo", which keeps the top note light. Watch where your top note lands on the staff.
Then switch the tune off and sing it from memory over the chords. Ideas: sing it on "ng", or hold the top note one beat longer.

Press Start exercise below, then sing the highlighted notes on "ah", one long note per chord: {{4}} over Dm7, {{4}} over G7, {{3}} over Cmaj7. Then the other line: {{1}} over Dm7, {{7}} over G7, {{7}} over Cmaj7. The root of each chord is lit too.
Now try it with no chords. Sing the same notes, and find each chord in your head before you sing it. Ideas: sing it on "ee" or "mm", slow it down, or start from the top note and go down.

Press Start exercise below to start the mic and the same changes in F: Gm7, C7, Fmaj7. The notes change, the pattern doesn't. Make up your own line on any vowel, starting each chord on one of its lit notes: {{4}} or {{1}} over Gm7, {{7}} or {{4}} over C7, {{3}} or {{7}} over Fmaj7. You can dip to {{7}} under the low {{1}} too. Leave space between phrases.
